articles.title: Eurozone bond yields fall as lower energy prices ease inflation concerns
articles.content: On Tuesday, government bond yields in the Eurozone experienced a notable drop, particularly for French and Italian bonds. The easing of inflation worries, attributed to falling oil and natural gas prices, enhanced demand for bonds. Germany's 10-year bond yield fell to 3.25%, while France's decreased to 4.69%. Boosted by the US President's calming remarks, market sentiment improved, especially for nations that had faced challenges in their bond markets.

articles.content: India's central bank has informed some lenders about the need to adjust bond forward accounting practices. articles.title: Oil falls as Trump downplays prospect of escalation with Iran
articles.content: Oil prices fell due to President Trump's announcement regarding US military action against Iran, easing supply concerns. Brent crude futures dropped to $92.33 per barrel while WTI futures reached $86.50. Trump stated he would maintain a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz temporarily. OPEC's oil output increased in October, supported by higher production from Saudi Arabia and Kuwait.

articles.title: Trump administration's embrace of "perp" futures sets off risk alarms for Wall Street stalwarts
articles.content: The decision by the Trump administration to launch perpetual futures has sparked significant worry among market stakeholders. Leaders from established exchanges contend that these offerings might disrupt existing market dynamics and risk assessment practices. They claim that perpetual futures ought to be categorized as swaps due to their unique trading characteristics. Moreover, ongoing trading raises alarm about liquidity and counterparty risk, especially in turbulent market conditions.
